name: Radboud Scholarship Programme
summary: A partial scholarship that cuts the tuition fee for a full English-taught master's at Radboud University. It also covers visa, residence permit and insurance costs, but not living costs.
eligibilityNotes: Open to holders of a non-EU/non-EEA passport who do not qualify for the lower EU/EEA tuition fee for other reasons. Bachelor's degree must be from outside the Netherlands, with no prior Dutch education. Must be fully admitted to an English-taught Radboud master's starting 1 September 2027. Erasmus Mundus and joint-degree programmes are excluded. Maximum 26 scholarships. The page gives an example where tuition falls to about 2,771 EUR (to be confirmed), so the exact award is not published as a single figure.
deadlineNote: Submit the OSIRIS application by 31 January 2027 and make it complete by 14 February 2027. Decisions expected before mid-April 2027.

name: Amsterdam Merit Scholarship (Economics and Business bachelor)
provider: University of Amsterdam, Faculty of Economics and Business
summary: A merit scholarship for outstanding non-EU students starting a bachelor in Economics and Business at the University of Amsterdam. A limited number are awarded each year.
eligibilityNotes: The programme page says outstanding students from outside the EU can apply (excluded list is the EU/EEA/EFTA codes). Programme page gives 6,000 EUR per year (18,000 EUR in total); the faculty scholarship page says amounts are set yearly and published in late autumn, so check the current figure. Pays by reimbursement, not a tuition waiver. Requires excellent grades (about 90-100% or A to A+), no entitlement to Dutch study finance, no other full scholarship, and admission to the programme via Studielink.
deadlineNote: Faculty page lists 15 January (Business Administration, Economics and Business Economics) and 1 March (other Economics and Business bachelors) but does not state the year; confirm the 2027 entry date. Results announced end of April.

name: Amsterdam Merit Scholarship (Graduate School of Social Sciences)
provider: University of Amsterdam, Graduate School of Social Sciences
summary: A scholarship equal to the tuition fee for non-EU/EEA students admitted to selective English-taught master's programmes at the Graduate School of Social Sciences. Very few are awarded (two in 2025).
eligibilityNotes: Requires a non-EU/EEA passport, no entitlement to Dutch study grants/loans or the low tuition fee, and full admission to an eligible English-taught selective GSSS master's. Amount equals the tuition fee, which is not published as a single number. Exclusion list is EU/EEA/EFTA codes.
deadlineNote: No later than 15 February 2027, 23:59 CET; late applications are not accepted.
